PullRequest.Title: agentHost: expand runtime E2E and enterprise tests
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary
- Add **207 supported Agent Host E2E cases**, including all **42 enterprise scenarios**, with strict tokenless model replay and real provider/AHP/tool execution. Keep 141 declarations in the PR profile and 66 SDK-native depth/stress declarations Full-only. Existing platform, record-only, and known-issue gates remain unchanged.
- Isolate every synthetic workspace outside the repository using the existing canonical directory helper, preventing mutable repository instructions/skills from changing recorded test behavior. Add a regression guard for this invariant.
- Give native web spill output a unique canonical directory per test; verify two simultaneous exact-output replays cannot share or delete each other's files.
- Keep the two mandatory Copilot workers complementary and scheduled first. **No timeout or concurrency increase**, no weakened replay/side-effect assertions, and no new skip to hide the current failures.
- **No GitHub/Azure pipeline YAML changes remain in the PR.** The earlier Azure pre-integration phase became redundant when upstream introduced dedicated Agent Host jobs. Remove that phase and the common checkpoint extension; a regression now requires exactly one Agent Host test step and its own checkpoint per platform.

## Current failure fixes
The current red CI was deterministic rather than an unchanged-input flaky retry:
- Remove 26 obsolete LSP scenarios and 52 generated artifacts rather than adding LSP to the production tool budget. Upstream intentionally left it off in [#342336](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/342336). Both supported plugin skill/resource cases remain.
- Follow current managed Assisted semantics from [#341889](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/341889). Assisted remains available under a bypass lock but cannot weaken managed denials. The replacement checks repeated real denials and AHP effective/available modes. Separate manual/Allow All tests still require human, one-time approval.
- Update the empty allowlist case to assert native and registered client tools are absent, matching current host/source filtering. Other positive client-tool routing/schema/result tests remain enabled.
- Re-record the one shell patch/retest fixture that had accidentally invoked this repository's mutable `unit-tests` skill. The test now runs the same real command, sees the real failure, applies the exact patch, reruns unchanged tests, and verifies the side effect without inheriting repository customizations.

## CI history and flakiness review
A bounded review of prior GitHub/ADO logs confirmed that earlier new tests did fail: path and shell portability, FSEvents mutation races, incidental snapshot ordering, MCP hot re-enable, SDK assertion drift, and test-phase timeouts. These were not all unrelated infrastructure failures. Existing normalization/readiness/synchronization fixes are retained; obsolete native LSP tests are removed rather than gated.

The reviewed history did **not** establish a named newly added test that failed and passed on an unchanged-input GitHub retry. The existing SDK canvas-resume test did. This does not establish zero flake risk; repeated current-head execution is the acceptance evidence below. Historical green runs selected Full, not the lighter profile.

## Final validation
Head **`f62d277e201e1eb62ce57f814768416d69f7294f`**, SDK **`1.0.23-preview.5`**, after normal merge of main through `fce724a39c3dbc8fadcb4829823f374b929344bd`.

- **[Code OSS CI 39363671343](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/39363671343): SUCCESS**, including Compile & Hygiene and Linux/macOS/Windows Electron jobs.
- **[Azure 486589](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=486589): overall SUCCESS** on final head, with exactly one actual dedicated Agent Host job per platform. Remaining integration jobs also pass.
- **[Azure 486575](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=486575): overall SUCCESS** on `031653041b7`. Its dedicated Agent Host tasks provide the first clean independent execution with identical case/runtime/fixture inputs. Extra obsolete integration-prestep executions in that build are **not** counted. The final commit only removes redundant pipeline orchestration and adds its guard/documentation.

| Accepted Full execution | Windows x64 | Linux x64 | macOS ARM64 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 486575 dedicated Agent Host tasks | Passed | Passed | Passed |
| 486589 dedicated Agent Host tasks, final head | Passed | Passed | Passed |

Both runs explicitly selected Full. Each platform executed all 153 enabled runtime cases and every supported enterprise variant; Windows also executed its documented shell-read variant. Existing pending counts remained 12 on Windows / 13 on Linux and macOS. Linux executed its required disk-backed lifecycle pass in both runs. No checkpoint/cache skip is counted as an execution.

### Build-time impact
Final measured **total Agent Host phase** walltime (not claimed incremental overhead versus a matched pre-PR baseline):

| Platform | GitHub Code OSS | Azure packaged |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Linux | 7m23s | 5m49s |
| macOS | 6m44s | 5m31s |
| Windows | 23m16s | 21m24s |

These are within the unchanged upstream deadlines. Ordinary implementation PRs use the smaller PR profile under upstream change detection; test/fixture changes intentionally force Full. Removing the obsolete Azure prestep eliminates a second complete Agent Host run from each platform's remaining-integration job.

### Local checks
- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — passed.
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- `npm run eslint -- <changed TypeScript files>` — passed.
- `node --test build\lib\testAgentHostE2EStartup.test.ts build\lib\test\agentHostTestSelection.test.ts build\lib\test\testCheckpointTemplates.test.ts` — 31 passed, including canonical/out-of-checkout fixture isolation and once-only packaged execution.
- `scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\e2e\providers\copilotAgentHostE2E.integrationTest.ts --grep 'runtime coverage|managed settings'` with `AGENT_HOST_TEST_PROFILE=full` — **196 passed / 12 existing pending** (195 task-added enabled Windows cases plus one matching upstream case).
- Same selection with `AGENT_HOST_TEST_PROFILE=pr` — **139 passed / 69 existing/profile pending**.
- Five unchanged repetitions of seven sensitive/corrected cases — **35/35 passed**, covering MCP hot re-enable, compacted-context restart, managed policy denial, empty allowlist, shell patch/retest, and both plugin resources.
- Two simultaneous web pagination/spill cases — **2/2 passed** with exact content/limits and AHP full-output recovery.
- Three unchanged executions of the shared snapshot/path/proxy selection — **36/36 passed each time**, 108 passes total.

A complete local run also reproduced existing debug-log availability and Windows temporary-home cleanup failures; exact isolated debug retries retained those failures. Those unrelated assertions were not changed, and final GitHub/Azure runs pass their complete suites.

## Scope
No new runtime coverage collector, tooling tests, npm command, tracked metrics report, generated HTML, instrumentation binary, private runtime source, or raw profile is included. Existing upstream coverage infrastructure is unchanged. Earlier local diagnostic native coverage numbers are not presented as current stability evidence.

(Written by Copilot)

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The runner derives its default job count directly from suites.length, CI invokes it without --jobs, and the diff increases the suite array from six entries to seven by adding a second Copilot worker. On hosts exposing at least seven CPUs, all seven suite subprocesses therefore start concurrently; exact contention severity depends on runner capacity, but the mechanism and trigger are direct.
Findings.PerformanceResource: one additional concurrent Electron test process plus its Agent Host/provider subprocesses, CPU, memory, and filesystem I/O
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Default concurrency is min(suites.length, availableParallelism); this added suite raises the aggregate from 6 to 7 workers whenever availableParallelism is at least 7, including the normal unqualified CI invocations.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: higher peak CPU and memory pressure and I/O contention, which can reduce test throughput or cause timeouts/OOMs on shared CI agents
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The six-entry suite array made the default runner start at most six suite subprocesses; Copilot coverage used one worker.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The added copilot-runtime suite creates a seventh independently spawned process, and the unchanged default-jobs calculation now permits seven concurrent workers.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added `id: 'copilot-runtime'` suite at RIGHT line 64 is a new independently spawned suite; with the unchanged `defaultJobs = Math.min(suites.length, availableParallelism...)`, it increases default process concurrency by one.
Findings.Title: Keep the split worker within the existing concurrency cap
Findings.Impact: Running the standard Agent Host E2E command in GitHub/Azure or locally on a machine with at least seven CPUs now launches seven heavyweight workers at once rather than six. Each worker starts Electron-backed tests and Agent Host/provider processes, increasing peak resource contention even though the Copilot title filters are disjoint.
Findings.Evidence: CI scripts call runner.ts without --jobs, parseArguments computes defaultJobs as min(suites.length, availableParallelism), and main creates exactly jobs concurrent workers that each call runSuite/spawn. The changed suite array adds copilot-runtime while retaining all prior entries, so the default aggregate rises from six to seven.
Findings.Recommendation: Preserve the split and coverage but cap the implicit default at the previous six workers (or pass an explicit six-worker cap from CI); keep higher concurrency an explicit --jobs opt-in.

Scenarios.Scenario: Standard Agent Host E2E run in GitHub/Azure or locally
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Runtime preparation completes first, then every suite must finish before results are merged and the test phase can pass. CI invokes the runner without an explicit worker cap.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Spawn one test process per suite, which transitively launches Electron-backed Agent Host/provider processes
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: 7 suite subprocesses concurrently on hosts with >=7 CPUs, versus 6 before the diff
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One Copilot worker and six total suite entries limited default aggregate concurrency to six.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All suite subprocesses must complete; the extra simultaneous worker increases peak CPU/memory/I/O contention and can reduce throughput on constrained agents.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read/write temporary workspaces, replay fixtures, logs, protocol-surface outputs, and Linux resource diagnostics
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Bounded per test and per worker, but now up to seven workers issue this I/O concurrently by default
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same classes of I/O existed, with at most six default concurrent workers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Fixture and workspace I/O is on each worker's critical path; aggregate contention is amplified by the added worker.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of suite entries and available CPUs; the diff changes the effective suite cardinality from 6 to 7, so hosts with at least 7 available CPUs run 7 workers concurrently.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: `defaultJobs = min(suites.length, availableParallelism)` and a shared queue feeds exactly `jobs` async workers. Before the diff the maximum default was 6; after adding `copilot-runtime` it is 7. The two Copilot partitions are disjoint but are separate concurrent processes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Electron installation/preparation is checked once before workers. Each worker has an isolated cold test process and provider host; within a provider suite replay mode reuses a warm server until test/model-backed thresholds or environment changes force recycling. The extra worker cannot share those per-process caches.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: suite count, default-jobs formula, unqualified CI invocation, worker queue, and spawn path are all directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact slowdown or memory peak depends on CI machine capacity and availableParallelism; this affects severity, not the proven increase from six to seven heavyweight workers.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable concurrency-burst regression; preserve the split but retain the previous implicit six-worker cap.

Scenarios.Scenario: Deterministic replay of individual Copilot runtime and enterprise cases
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A worker loads the shared Copilot entrypoint, Mocha title filtering selects one partition, setup acquires/reuses or recycles the Agent Host server, local replay HTTP serves recorded model turns, and assertions/snapshot serialization finish before the next serial test.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load YAML replay fixtures and create/remove canonical temporary workspaces, files, git repositories, spill outputs, and telemetry files
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Generally one fixture/workspace per selected test; large native data/shell/web cases are Full-only, while enterprise scenarios remain PR-enabled
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The harness already performed fixture and workspace I/O for existing cases; the diff adds bounded new scenarios and keeps native depth Full-only.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Workspace and fixture operations are on test setup/tool/assertion paths but bounded by declared test cases and profile gates.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Loopback HTTP between provider, replay proxy, MCP/web/OAuth/OTLP fixture servers, and AHP client/server
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Bounded by each scripted scenario and recorded model-turn count; no external network in replay
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Replay already used a local CAPI proxy; the diff adds scoped loopback fixture endpoints for new coverage.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Loopback responses drive the test turn and are on its critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Recycle the Agent Host/provider process when a test-specific environment differs or existing reuse limits are reached; selected shell/MCP tests also launch bounded local commands
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One recycle per transition between distinct environment maps; tests sharing identical maps reuse the process. Full-only shell/data depth bounds the heaviest subprocess work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Threshold-based recycling existed; environment-based invalidation and new bounded subprocess scenarios are added.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Launch/recycle is awaited before a test proceeds; this is required for process-level environment semantics.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Normalize model/AHP traffic, saved-output paths, fixture URLs, and serialize snapshots
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per recorded/replayed request and captured snapshot string/object; bindings/maps reset between fixtures
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Traffic normalization/serialization already existed; the diff adds bounded URL and spill-path passes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Normalization and serialization occur before strict replay comparison or snapshot assertion, but remain bounded by captured traffic.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Selected profile and title cardinality: PR runs the supported host/enterprise subset; Full adds native depth/stress cases. Within a worker tests are serial, with server reuse bounded by existing test/model-backed thresholds.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One test at a time inside each Copilot worker; the runner may execute the ordinary and runtime partitions concurrently. Local fixture servers are scoped to their test and disposed after turns drain.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Replay fixtures are loaded per test into a shared proxy; replay buckets, placeholder bindings, ancillary responses, observations, and saved-output maps are cleared on reset. Agent Host/provider state is warm within reuse thresholds. Test environment changes deliberately invalidate reuse and recycle the server; contiguous tests sharing the same environment reuse it.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the execution path and lifecycle; no additional unbounded fan-out, retention, or concurrency was found within a worker.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact per-case durations and provider process launch costs vary by platform, but profile gates, serial execution within each worker, reset semantics, and boundary cardinalities are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional reportable regression. Added work is intentional test coverage, heavy native cases are Full-only, resources are scoped/reset, and environment recycling preserves required process semantics.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: A focused provider command starts a fresh replay proxy/server per test, forwards model requests to the configured upstream, drains in-flight recordings, writes fixtures/snapshots, and only then completes teardown.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Forward recorded model endpoint requests to the upstream provider and drain responses
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One or more upstream requests per explicitly recorded turn; no aggregate complete-suite parallel recording
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Recording already forwarded provider requests and used fresh proxies; new scenarios use the same controlled path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Upstream completion and the bounded 30-second drain are required before fixture writing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write model capture YAML and AHP snapshots
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One output fixture/snapshot per selected case
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same write mechanism existed; the diff adds more committed fixtures and normalization placeholders.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Writes complete during teardown/assertion before the recording command succeeds.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Explicitly selected recording tests and model-turn count; these modes are rejected by the parallel complete-suite runner and are normally run per provider/focused selection.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Parallel runner validation rejects recording and snapshot-update flags. Recording therefore remains focused/serial rather than multiplying external requests across the seven workers.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Recording intentionally does not reuse the shared replay server; each test gets fresh fixture state. Generated URL/token/path bindings are scoped to a fixture and disposables/reset prevent cross-test reuse.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: mode gates, fresh-server behavior, network forwarding, drain, and write paths are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: External provider latency varies, but this workflow is explicit, focused, and isolated from the changed default worker concurrency.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; external boundary work scales with intentionally selected recording cases and remains non-parallel.

Scenarios.Scenario: Static build/unit guards for selection, checkpoints, normalization, and fixture isolation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Node tests synchronously read runner/pipeline/suite files, parse TypeScript/YAML, and execute bounded local HTTP/filesystem regression cases before the build-test job completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read suite, runner, and pipeline files; parse AST/YAML; create/remove temporary replay fixtures
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One pass over runtime suite files and three platform templates plus fixed regression cases
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Selection tests already read repository metadata; the diff adds fixed-count guards and cases.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous reads/parsing are on the unit-test critical path but bounded to repository test metadata.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start loopback HTTP servers/proxies for replay normalization tests
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Fixed number of local test servers and requests
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The test file already exercised local replay proxy behavior; the diff adds bounded cases.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each test awaits local responses and closes servers before completion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Repository suite-file count and fixed platform list; the new isolation guard scans runtime coverage suite sources once, while normalization tests use fixed cases.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Node test runner scheduling applies; the changed loops themselves are synchronous and bounded, with no new uncontrolled worker pool.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No persistent cache is introduced. Files are read once per relevant assertion; temporary directories and local servers are removed/closed in test cleanup.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for bounded behavior; no realistic scaling or lifecycle leak was found.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Added unit-test wall time is not measured separately, but all loops and local boundaries have small fixed cardinality.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete 281-file inventory, executable harness/runner/suite diffs, generated fixtures, snapshots, and affected CI entrypoints. Submitted one performance finding: the added Copilot runtime suite raises uncapped default worker concurrency from six to seven. Test-specific environment recycling, replay normalization, fixture URL/saved-output maps, and added full/PR cases were traced but did not establish additional high-confidence regressions beyond intentional bounded test work.
